title: Insulin Pump Program Patient Account Terms by Tier
content:
These are the patient-account figures of the Insulin Pump Program for each tier: payment plans, the past-due shipment hold, small balances, hardship assistance and credit refunds.

## Payment plans and the past-due hold

| Tier | Minimum balance for a payment plan | Maximum plan months | Minimum monthly installment | Past-due age (days) | Past-due hold minimum |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Insulin Pump Self-Pay Program | $150.00 | 0 (no payment plans) | $25.00 | 15 | $50.00 |
| Insulin Pump Commercial HMO Program | $150.00 | 6 | $25.00 | 90 | $75.00 |
| Insulin Pump Commercial PPO Program | $150.00 | 6 | $25.00 | 90 | $75.00 |
| Insulin Pump Medicare Advantage Program | $100.00 | 10 | $20.00 | 120 | $75.00 |
| Insulin Pump Original Medicare Program | $100.00 | 10 | $20.00 | 120 | $75.00 |
| Insulin Pump Medicaid Program | $100.00 | 0 (no payment plans) | $20.00 | 0 (never held for a past-due balance) | $75.00 |

## Write-offs, hardship and credits

| Tier | Small-balance write-off ceiling | Hardship waiver may be granted | Hardship income ceiling | Credit-balance refund limit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Insulin Pump Self-Pay Program | $0.00 (none) | No | 200% of the guideline | 30 days |
| Insulin Pump Commercial HMO Program | $4.99 | Yes | 200% of the guideline | 30 days |
| Insulin Pump Commercial PPO Program | $4.99 | Yes | 200% of the guideline | 30 days |
| Insulin Pump Medicare Advantage Program | $4.99 | Yes | 200% of the guideline | 60 days |
| Insulin Pump Original Medicare Program | $0.00 (none) | Yes | 200% of the guideline | 60 days |
| Insulin Pump Medicaid Program | $0.00 (none) | No | 200% of the guideline | 60 days |

## What the figures mean

- **Minimum balance for a payment plan** — the smallest patient balance, in US dollars, for which an interest-free payment plan may be requested.
- **Maximum plan months** — the longest interest-free payment plan, in monthly installments; 0 means payment plans are not offered on the tier.
- **Minimum monthly installment** — the smallest monthly installment accepted on a payment plan, in US dollars.
- **Past-due age** — the age, in calendar days after its posting date, at which an unpaid patient-balance posting becomes past due for the shipment hold test; 0 means shipments are never held for a past-due balance on the tier.
- **Past-due hold minimum** — the past-due amount, in US dollars, at or above which further shipments are held under the past-due rule.
- **Small-balance write-off ceiling** — the largest remaining patient balance, in US dollars, that is written off as a small balance instead of being statemented; $0.00 means no small-balance write-off on the tier.
- **Hardship waiver may be granted** — whether a documented financial-hardship waiver of patient cost share may be granted case by case on the tier.
- **Hardship income ceiling** — the household income ceiling for a financial-hardship waiver, as a percent of the current HHS federal poverty guideline for the household size; an integer percent.
- **Credit-balance refund limit** — the time limit for refunding a customer credit balance (overpayment), in calendar days counted from the posting date of the entry that created the credit.

*Illustration (hypothetical):* a program on a tier with a $100.00 minimum balance and a $20.00 minimum installment, carrying a $90.00 balance, is below that tier's payment-plan minimum; at $100.00 it reaches it.
